texts: us family considering uk move via ancestry visa hi all looking for perspective from people whove actually made this leap or seriously considered it my wife has a clear path to a uk ancestry visa through her grandmother who immigrated to the us from southampton her family heritage is very ukrooted and that connection has always mattered to her this wouldnt be a random move to a place weve never experienced weve visited the uk multiple times including with our two boys now 7 and 13 and genuinely loved it the culture pace of life history walkability public transport schools and just the general feel and very inline with what we love the boys would be completely on board with the move which honestly surprised us in a good way the complication is that to make the ancestry visa possible for our whole family wed likely need to pursue citizenship by investment in a commonwealth country which would cost us somewhere in the 90k150k range thats a huge financial and emotional commitment and not something we take lightly whats really giving us pause isnt whether wed enjoy life in the uk we know we would but the gravity of what wed be leaving behind selling our home selling or storing most of our belongings leaving family friends and a life weve spent years building accepting that this isnt just trying something new but potentially burning the ships behind us at the same time were genuinely scared about the current and future political climate in the us that fear isnt the only reason were considering this as weve talked about living in the uk before things felt this tense but it has absolutely accelerated the conversation it feels like one of those moments where you either act on what youve been thinking for yearsor you dont so im hoping to hear from people whove been in a similar position did you struggle with the idea of leaving behind your old life even if the new one was good how did your kids adapt longterm not just the honeymoon phase did the financial and logistical cost feel worth it a few years in if you moved partly out of concern for the us did that fear ease or just change shape knowing what you know now would you still do it were trying hard to separate emotion from reality but this feels like one of those decisions where logic only gets you so far also we would keep a lake cottage we have here and intend to travel back for a few weeks every summer where wed be able to see familyfriends appreciate any honest experiences good bad or mixed

advice for a young artist hello everyone im searching for some general personal advice from people all over who i ask this to people in the film industry or artists alike people who are expats after graduation and people who may have insights on the matter i ask my problem ive just graduated with a bachelors in film tv and video in belgium but am thinking of perhaps moving away from this country due to personal reasons its just an idea for now nothing is set in stone but im in a sortof researching phase to discover whats out there the problem i think most people right now have is that the climate of most countries is highly impossible to properly livemove to as a youngster high rents competitive job market making it impossible changing politics and other things yet i remain hopeful to open my wings and move out of my own country my field film isnt that big here compared to other neighbouring places and quite hard to even get a job in it without nepotism or a million pa jobs on unpaid internships our government doesnt truly respect art to fund it well enough imo and people here are living in a specific nihilistic mindset ive grown tired of my experience i know what a badly ironic view haha logically there are some good things perhaps even advantages i take for granted but as said even with those the personal reasons are urging me to maybe move in the next few years my research has pingponged me from one place to another slovenia uk france czech wherever but im at such a loss for where to actually focus it seems with every pick the more i delve into it the more i start doubting if its the correct one im young inexperienced beyond the experience that i have and eager to start my own career and life and work for it to get it i realise what a wide world there is and that it is a matter of daring more than planning in a world where a million people struggle with the same how does one break ones own cycle so i ask all of you the following your advice and experiences how is your country for those in a similar field or inside the film industry im looking for a place region andor country i can focus on making my art whilst also doing some parttime or other work i dont want much as in id be happy to just go live there with my dog and do some local job whilst i start my own stuff no place is perfect i know that but there are places that benefit specific individuals more than others im searching for the correct guidance and who better to ask than people who actually live there i dont have a set of criteria ill put here just so i can hear the stories you all have without demanding answers so please if anyone has anything they could share id be happy to listen hope this is clear enough i know its a famous question probably but i thought to just try it a wise friend of mine once told me my future lies outside the confines of my village and i intend to chase that dream until the bitter end even if itll cost me a limb and all my courage i just need to know where in this continent or outside that is thank you regards

how to choose the right healthcare logistics company in india the healthcare and pharmaceutical industry operates under strict quality safety and regulatory expectations logistics plays a critical role in ensuring that medicines vaccines and medical products reach patients in the right condition even a small lapse in handling or temperature control can lead to product damage regulatory penalties and serious risks to patient health this is why selecting the right healthcare logistics company in india is not a routine vendor decision it is a strategic choice that directly impacts product integrity compliance and brand trust why healthcare logistics requires specialised expertise healthcare logistics is fundamentally different from general cargo or retail distribution pharmaceutical products are highly sensitive to environmental conditions and handling practices many medicines injectables vaccines and diagnostic samples require strict temperature control throughout storage and transportation experienced pharma cold chain logistics companies understand these complexities they operate with defined sops trained personnel validated packaging and continuous monitoring systems a logistics partner without healthcarespecific experience can unintentionally compromise product quality at any stage of the supply chain importance of cold chain infrastructure in pharma logistics cold chain capability is the backbone of healthcare logistics a reliable cold chain logistics company in india must ensure uninterrupted temperature control during warehousing transportation and lastmile delivery this includes chilled controlled ambient and frozen movements based on product requirements temperature stability must be maintained regardless of transit distance climate conditions or delivery location any break in the cold chain can result in loss of potency product rejection or noncompliance role of technology in healthcare logistics technology has become essential in modern healthcare logistics operations realtime shipment tracking temperature monitoring and digital reporting provide visibility and accountability across the supply chain a capable healthcare logistics partner should offer live temperature data automated alerts for deviations and posttrip reports for quality and audit purposes these systems help businesses identify risks early take corrective action and maintain compliance with regulatory standards compliance and regulatory readiness regulatory compliance is nonnegotiable in healthcare logistics logistics partners must follow gdpaligned practices and maintain proper documentation traceability and handling protocols a dependable healthcare logistics company india operates with audit readiness at all times compliance is embedded into daily operations not treated as an occasional requirement clear documentation trained staff and defined escalation processes are key indicators of compliance maturity secure warehousing and risk management pharmaceutical products require controlled and secure storage environments warehouses must be equipped with temperature control systems contamination prevention measures and safety protocols to protect sensitive goods security is equally important medicines are highvalue products and vulnerable to theft or counterfeiting strong access controls surveillance systems and process discipline help reduce these risks and ensure product safety during storage network strength and location advantage an effective healthcare supply chain depends on network reach healthcare logistics often involves deliveries beyond metro cities to hospitals clinics laboratories and distributors across tier 2 and tier 3 locations a strong logistics partner should have the infrastructure and operational capability to manage longdistance and lastmile deliveries without compromising temperature or handling standards strategic presence near manufacturing hubs and healthcare centers improves delivery efficiency and reduces transit risks balancing cost with service quality while cost is an important consideration healthcare logistics decisions should never be driven by price alone lowercost services may result in delays temperature deviations or compliance failures that cost far more in the long run the right partner focuses on reliability transparency and longterm value rather than shortterm savings consistent service quality protects both business continuity and patient safety customer support and operational transparency healthcare logistics requires proactive communication delays route changes or environmental risks must be communicated immediately a dedicated support team and clear escalation structure ensure that issues are addressed before they impact product quality transparent communication builds trust and enables better coordination between logistics teams quality departments and customers future of healthcare logistics in india healthcare logistics continues to evolve with advancements in technology and process automation datadriven planning predictive analytics and integrated monitoring systems are shaping the future of pharmaceutical supply chains companies that invest in modern infrastructure and digital tools are better positioned to meet growing regulatory demands and rising expectations for speed accuracy and compliance choosing the right partner for healthcare logistics selecting the right healthcare logistics company in india is a critical business decision the ideal partner combines healthcarespecific experience cold chain expertise regulatory readiness and strong operational transparency a dependable logistics provider supports not only efficient delivery but also compliance risk reduction and patient safety making them a true extension of your healthcare supply chain conclusion choosing the right healthcare logistics company in india is essential for protecting product quality ensuring compliance and maintaining patient safety with healthcare logistics there is no room for error stc courier delivers reliable cold chain logistics backed by process discipline temperature control and nationwide reach making it a dependable partner for pharmaceutical and healthcare supply chains across india

i asked are there enough resources to provide decent quality of life for every body on the planet decent housing decent health decent education short answer yes in physical and technical terms there are enough resources long answer we dont organize them that way lets break it down cleanly and honestly 1 housing yes easily the world already produces enough building materials to house everyone there are more empty homes than unhoused people in many countries modular prefab and localmaterial construction can deliver durable housing at low cost the barrier is not materials its land ownership models speculation zoning and profitfirst real estate systems 2 food health yes decisively we produce 15 more food than needed to feed the global population most hunger is caused by distribution failures conflict and poverty not scarcity basic healthcare vaccinations maternal care sanitation primary medicine is cheap relative to global gdp a large share of preventable deaths come from lack of clean water lack of basic clinics lack of early intervention all solvable with existing tech and money 3 education yes overwhelmingly digital infrastructure teachers open curricula can provide highquality basic education globally literacy numeracy and vocational skills do not require elite universities countries with far fewer resources than the global average have achieved nearuniversal literacy the real issue is political will and priorities not capability 4 energy infrastructure yes with transition renewable energy potential alone solar wind hydro exceeds global demand many times over energy poverty persists because of upfront investment gaps not lack of energy sources distributed systems microgrids local water treatment community internet already work 5 so why doesnt everyone have a decent life because our global system is optimized for profit maximization wealth concentration shortterm national advantage power preservation not for human wellbeing this is not a conspiracy its structural inertia the uncomfortable truth we already choose scarcity where abundance exists globally a small fraction of military spending could fund universal basic services a modest tax on extreme wealth could eradicate extreme poverty food waste alone could feed hundreds of millions but those choices threaten entrenched interests the deeper layer and this may resonate with you the crisis is not resourcebased its consciousnessbased we havent collectively decided that every human life is worth dignified care until that moral agreement exists the system will keep producing inequality even with abundance bottom line yes earth has enough resources yes we have the technology yes we have the labor and knowledge what we lack is collective alignment not capacity if you want 31yo im done running from myself and im ready to embrace who ive always been but im scared hello everyone im 31 years old and ive finally stopped running away from myself since i was 6 there have been signs that perhaps i dont have much in common with the gender i was assigned at birth for years and until a few months ago i ignored all those signs that appeared from time to time i told myself it was just a phase or even a kind of fetish that i could keep to myself although deep down i knew something was going on i thought that if i ignored it that voice would eventually disappear but it didnt sometimes it faded for a while but it always came back and when it did it came back stronger more persistent more real a few months ago it returned intensely and i told myself thats it something has to be done about it i realized that many moments in my life have always been conditioned by that without me realizing it or without wanting to realize it and suddenly a dysphoria has emerged with many physical characteristics id never felt before as well as a certain discomfort even towards hegemonic masculinity and its labels i realize that i inhabited masculinity but in a somewhat detached way because although i never truly fit into it it was a form of survival because it was what i was expected to be now the egg has broken and i cant and dont want to ignore the fact that most likely and almost certainly i am and always have been a woman accepting it and wanting to embrace it one and for all feels comforting like a weight has been lifted from my shoulders but at the same time i also feel very dizzy i want to embrace the femininity ive always felt within me but denied and im slowly experimenting with small invisible changes in my body and routine just to find some peace but the fear is overwhelming i still live with my parents although i believe deep down they would support me im terrified of seeing disappointment in their eyes or that something might change between us ive spent so much time being what they expected that the idea of showing them who i truly am feels like a betrayal to them i suppose thats how i was raised and its hard to break free from that on the other hand in the current social climate im afraid that choosing to be happy could mean losing my livelihood and the stability ive worked so hard to build im terrified that transphobia will ruin me professionally even though i know its a possibility i must face if i want to embrace who i am i also have a partner who supports me in all of this but were both afraid i love her and the idea that our relationship might change too much or even end because of my transitionbecause ive changed too much or shes stopped being attracted to mefills me with anxiety i look at your timelines and experiences your happiness being who you truly are and i feel so much hope but then i look at my own life and i feel paralyzed how do you manage the fear of losing everything youve built for me this is another important step discovering myself and freeing myself within a community even if its online thank you for being there im glad i can finally write this

crows and pigeons dying in large numbers in anantapur due to avian influenza india times of india telugu google translation crows are dying continuously at sku in anantapur falling suddenly from the trees what exactly is happening an alarming situation has arisen at sri krishnadevaraya university in anantapur district for the past three days a large number of crows have been dying on the university campus a similar situation prevails in the vanamitra forest park area near the university where a large number of pigeons are also dying crows and pigeons are suddenly falling from trees and dying causing concern among the local residents officials suspect that the deaths of the birds are due to the influenza virus a kind of alarming atmosphere prevails on the campus of sri krishnadevaraya university located on the outskirts of anantapur city the sudden death of birds on the university campus for the past three days is causing serious concern locally dozens of crows are dying a similar situation exists on the sk university campus as well as in the nearby vanamitra forest park area pigeons are also dying there the fact that birds are suddenly falling from trees and dying is causing anxiety however officials say that the influenza virus is the cause upon receiving information about these strange deaths professor ravi prasad rao head of the botany and zoology departments at sk university inspected the site on saturday he examined the dead crows he stated that they are dying due to the influenza virus it is believed that the virus may have spread due to climate change or through other migratory birds he said that directly touching these dead birds could lead to respiratory problems and conjunctivitis he suggested burying or cremating them using sticks meanwhile a similar situation was recently observed in kerala a large number of crows died in kannur district following this officials intervened and conducted tests it was determined that they died due to the h5n1 virus however it was stated that the virus had not spread from the crows to other birds precautionary measures have also been taken in the area on the other hand h5n1 is an influenza virus it causes respiratory problems in birds officials say that there is a possibility of this virus spreading to humans if they directly touch the birds that have died due to it in this context they are advising that the dead birds should be buried in a deep pit or cremated

ancient wisdom in arborihorticulture insights from the puras x200b the ancient indian texts particularly the puras offer a rich tapestry of knowledge on arborihorticulture blending practical agriculture with spiritual and hygienic considerations these scriptures composed over centuries reflect a deep understanding of plant life that was integral to daily existence arborihorticulture as depicted in these works encompassed not just the cultivation of trees and shrubs but also their medicinal environmental and cultural significance drawing from vedic roots the puras expanded on earlier wisdom providing detailed guidelines for planting nurturing and classifying flora this knowledge was not isolated but intertwined with broader sciences like medicine and town planning emphasizing harmony between humans and nature the agni pura for instance outlines specific tree placements around homes to promote health illustrating how ancient indians viewed plants as guardians of wellbeing such practices highlight a sophisticated approach that predates modern horticulture by millennia where empirical observations met mythological narratives the brhat sahit complements this by detailing soil preparation and manuring techniques showing a scientific bent in what might seem like ritualistic advice overall these texts reveal a holistic system where arborihorticulture served both utilitarian and symbolic purposes fostering sustainable living in ancient societies in exploring the evolution of this knowledge one finds connections to earlier vedic literature the gveda and atharvaveda mention numerous medicinal plants laying the foundation for later puric elaborations by the time of the puras this had matured into a comprehensive science known as vkyurveda or the science of tree life kautilyas arthastra references the need for agricultural superintendents to be versed in this field underscoring its importance in state administration cities were envisioned with abundant gardens both artificial and natural to enhance aesthetics and health the puras prescribe planting trees like plaka in the north vaa in the east mra in the south and avattha in the west believing these orientations harnessed directional energies for human benefit such directives were not arbitrary but based on observed effects on air quality and microclimates the emphasis on spacingtwenty cubits for optimal growthreflects an understanding of resource competition among plants trees planted too closely were seen as yielding poor fruits a principle echoed in modern arboriculture manuring methods using fish washings or meat residues demonstrate innovative use of organic waste aligning with contemporary sustainable practices plant diseases were diagnosed through symptoms like leaf paleness or sap oozing with remedies involving herbal infusions showing a protopathological approach the classification of plants in the puras adds another layer of insight the vyu pura divides flora into categories like vka trees gulma shrubs lat creepers vall climbers and ta grasses a system that mirrors botanical taxonomies this genealogy is mythologized through kyapas progeny where daughters like lat and vall represent plant types flowers are categorized by color and scent with the matsya pura describing lotuses in hues resembling the sun moon or gold these descriptions served practical purposes aiding in identification for medicinal or ornamental use the mrkaeya pura outlines plant evolution from grass to tree suggesting an observational awareness of growth stages fumigation with hog flesh or deer meat for pest control indicates early integrated pest management irrigation with specific concoctions like clarified butter mixed with barley was believed to boost flowering and fruiting these techniques while rooted in tradition often have verifiable benefits such as nutrient enrichment from animalbased fertilizers the puras thus preserve a legacy of empirical knowledge passed down through generations that continues to inform ethnobotanical studies today hygienic and practical aspects of tree plantation the hygienic benefits of strategic touched was mandatory to avoid fruitlessness reflecting an understanding of canopy management the brhat sahit specifies distances of 18 to 30 feet varying by tree quality to optimize yield inferior trees could be closer but premium ones needed more space for root expansion such guidelines were practical for orchards and urban groves balancing productivity with aesthetics the ukranti echoes this i wish someone told me this before moving to ireland for studies upon arriving in ireland as an international student for pursuing my higher studies i wish id received the following advice to avoid stress financial loss and emotional strain i realized i was not fully prepared for the transition into a foreign country with distinctive cultural norms and markedly different climate conditions selecting the most suitable housing options has truly tested my patience it is necessary to look for accommodation months before you arrive there are a lot of shared houses which are normally available here but it will be difficult to get your dream room immediately if you are not getting suitable options as per your requirement be ready to compromise at first then upgrade later once you understand the area areas outside the city centre tallaght clondalkin saggart lucan finglas etc are cheaper and wellconnected by busesluas budgeting is essential in ireland ireland offers numerous attractive destinations although it is recognised as a relatively expensive country to visit aldi lidl are cheaper to shop groceries while dunnes stores and centra is much more expensive eating out regularly will drain your wallet faster than you think track your spending for the first 23 months youll be shocked where your money goes it is better not to convert everything into your home currency as it will drive you crazy later when you need money in ireland parttime jobs arent not easy to get a lot of students think theyll land a job in the first week but the reality is that it may take weeks or even months to find something you should have enough savings to survive at least for three or four months without income most of the employers look for previous experience as well as fulltime employees wherever you apply which the stamp does not allow irelands weather is unpredictable weather can change at any time always carry a small umbrella or waterproof jacket it is always better to check the weather prediction if you plan to explore places outside i arrived in ireland in may which is considered an ideal time for exploring the country subsequently autumn and then winter follow with winter being the present season transport is good but sometimes buses and trams can be late especially in winter students can always use leap card which will save the money for travel if you live near a luas line life becomes easier enjoy ireland beyond dublin there are many beautiful places outside dublin such as cork killarney howth cobh etc travel when ever you can as student life goes very fast never be afraid to ask for help being a student your college student union is always useful your college student services will always be there to help you out theres no shame in asking questions finally moving to ireland changed my life in the best ways but it wasnt easy if youre coming here for studies prepare well stay openminded and give yourself time to adjust

earth in a catastrophe cycle mythology and geology on global cataclysms myths and sacred texts from various cultures geographically distant from one another contain strikingly similar descriptions of events that go beyond ordinary floods or volcanic eruptions these are phenomena of a planetary scale the bible and the sumeroakkadian epic particularly the epic of gilgamesh describe a great flood that destroyed almost all of humanity egyptian traditions relayed to herodotus by priests speak of a time when the sun changed its usual position four times rising where it now sets and vice versa this could indicate a possible shift in the earths axis of rotation or a drastic change in its spatial orientation mesopotamian texts such as the prophecy the wrath of erra detail the horrors of a period of utter darkness the darkness was so thick it could not be dispelled by fire they describe the cessation of all biological processes famine and thirst hittite myths the wrath of telepinu the disappearance of the storm god paint a picture of ecological catastrophe suffocating smoke enveloping the earth the death of vegetation and the drying up of springs this aligns with signs of a nuclear winter that could have followed the impact of a large cosmic body or colossal eruptions these descriptions converge on key points a global flood days of darkness a suffocating atmosphere the displacement of celestial bodies such coincidence in independent sources suggests they are based on a collective memory of real experienced catastrophic events scientific data geology confirms catastrophes mythology finds unexpected confirmation in modern scientific data this is not about gradual changes but sudden catastrophic shifts that altered the planets appearance the younger dryas hypothesis approx 12800 years ago one of the most developed scenarios the geological boundary separating the pleistocene from the holocene is marked by layers containing nanodiamonds spherules soot and iridiumtraces characteristic of a large cosmic body impact or airbursts from cometary fragments this event coincided with a sharp cooling within decades the extinction of megafauna mammoths sabretoothed cats and the disappearance of the clovis culture in north america the 96k82k event approx 9600 or 8200 years ago another sharp episode of global cooling possibly triggered by the catastrophic discharge of freshwater from proglacial lakes in north america which disrupted thermohaline circulation in the atlantic cometasteroid impact circa 5200 years ago a number of researchers link this event to a sharp rise in sea levels recorded worldwide and the onset of a new wet period in the sahara this time is also marked by a cultural shift and the emergence of numerous flood myths in different regions the 42kiloyear event a global megadrought that became one of the factors or the main factor in the collapse of the old kingdom in egypt the akkadian empire in mesopotamia and the indus valley harappan civilization are catastrophes cyclical the identification of roughly 12000year intervals between some of these events younger dryas 128k years ago hypothetical event 52k years ago has given rise to the hypothesis of possible cyclicity this could be linked to the solar systems passage through dense clouds of interstellar dust close approaches with a hypothetical companion star nemesis or other galactic cycles thus the totality of datafrom universal myths of flood and darkness to specific geological findingsindicates that the calm stable development of civilizations is not a given the history of earth and humanity has been periodically interrupted by shock events that reshaped the world map the climate and the course of species development the question of the strict cyclicity of these events remains open but their reality forces us to seriously consider the fragility of our ecosystem and possible scenarios for the future

evaporate applying it immediately after short lukewarm showers not switching products every time she flared protecting her skin every day even when it looked fine slowly not overnight something remarkable happened the flareups became less frequent the itching and pain didnt rule her hours anymore she even noticed days where her skin actually stayed calm for longer than shed ever remembered limi valley trek walking into nepals last hidden himalayan valley the limi valley trek is one of nepals most remote and beautiful trekking journeys located in the far north west of the country close to the tibetan border the limi valley trek takes you into a world that feels untouched by time high mountains broad open valleys ancient monasteries and warmhearted people make limi valley a truly special place this trek is not about crowds or comfort it is about silence culture and a deep connection with nature for trekkers who want something different from the busy trails of everest and annapurna limi valley offers a rare and meaningful experience location and access limi valley lies in humla district one of nepals most isolated regions the valley sits at a high altitude mostly above 3600 meters and stretches along the northern border with tibet because of its location the landscape and culture feel more tibetan than nepali reaching limi valley is an adventure in itself the journey usually starts with a flight from kathmandu to nepalgunj followed by another flight to simikot the district headquarters of humla from simikot the trek continues on foot through rugged trails river valleys and high mountain passes the long and difficult access has helped keep the region quiet and unspoiled a trek away from the crowds one of the most attractive parts of the limi valley trek is its isolation very few trekkers visit this area each year days can pass without seeing another group on the trail instead of busy teahouses you walk through open land where only the sound of wind footsteps and distant prayer flags can be heard this quiet environment allows trekkers to slow down and truly experience the mountains the journey feels peaceful and personal making it ideal for people who enjoy solitude and reflection landscape and scenery the scenery of limi valley is vast dry and dramatic unlike the green hills of central nepal this region has a cold desert landscape with rocky slopes dry grasslands and vast open valleys snowcapped peaks rise in the distance while clear blue skies stretch endlessly above the trail crosses several high mountain passes offering breathtaking views from these passes trekkers can see long valleys distant himalayan ranges and the raw beauty of the highaltitude land rivers flow through deep gorges and small green fields appear like islands in the dry terrain wildlife can also be seen along the way blue sheep are common in the hills and birds of prey circle above although rare the area is also home to snow leopards making it even more special life and culture in limi valley the cultural experience of the limi valley trek is as powerful as the natural beauty the people of limi valley known as limi pa follow tibetan buddhism and live a traditional mountain lifestyle their lives are closely connected to nature animals and seasonal changes there are three main villages in the valley til halji and jang these villages are made of stone houses with flat roofs built to survive the harsh climate colorful prayer flags fly from rooftops and hillsides carrying prayers with the wind ancient monasteries are an essential part of village life halji monastery is one of the oldest monasteries in nepal and holds deep religious and historical value inside you can see old wall paintings statues and sacred texts the calm and spiritual atmosphere leaves a strong impression on visitors despite living in a harsh environment the local people are kind and welcoming they often invite trekkers into their homes for tea or simple meals sharing time with them offers insight into a life based on patience balance and respect trekking experience and difficulty the limi valley trek usually takes around 18 to 22 days depending on the chosen route and walking pace it is considered a challenging trek and is best suited for experienced trekkers the main challenges include high altitude long walking days and basic living conditions facilities are minimal and accommodation is often in tents or simple village homes food choices are nourishing yet straightforward usually made with local grains and vegetables several high passes must be crossed during the trek some reaching close to 5000 meters these sections are physically demanding but highly rewarding proper acclimatization and a steady pace are essential for safety and enjoyment best time to visit the best time to trek in the limi valley is from may to september during this period the weather is relatively stable and the high passes are more likely to be open summer brings warmer temperatures and occasional rain while the high plains become a colorful tapestry of wildflowers winter trekking is challenging due to heavy snow and freezing temperatures early spring can also be risky because mountain passes may still be blocked permits and preparation limi valley is a restricted area so special permits are required to enter trekkers must travel with a licensed guide and proper documents must be arranged in advance good preparation is crucial for this trek trekkers should be physically fit and have previous experience at high altitude warm clothing strong boots and reliable gear are essential because medical facilities are almost nonexistent carrying a first aid kit and having travel insurance with emergency evacuation coverage is strongly recommended responsible travel limi valley is a fragile and culturally rich region responsible trekking helps protect both the environment and the local way of life trekkers should avoid leaving waste respect religious sites and always ask before photographing people or monasteries using local guides and services helps support the community and ensures that tourism benefits the people who live there conclusion the limi valley trek is not an easy journey but it is gratifying it offers a rare chance to explore a hidden corner of the himalayas experience ancient tibetan culture and walk through landscapes that remain largely untouched for trekkers seeking true adventure quiet trails and meaningful cultural encounters limi valley is one of nepals most extraordinary trekking destinations it is not just a trek but a journey into a slower simpler and more peaceful world

world building advice non fantasy elements worldbuilding advice for nonfantasy elements 1 research and realism ground your world in thorough research and realism understand the historical cultural and geographical aspects relevant to your setting to create an authentic and believable environment 2 consider societal structures explore the societal structures and institutions that shape your world consider the political economic and social systems and examine how they influence the characters and plot 3 setting as a character treat the setting as a character in itself how does the environment impact the mood tone and dynamics of the story whether urban or rural the setting should contribute to the narrative in meaningful ways 4 timeline and history develop a timeline and history for your world considering significant events that have shaped the current state of affairs historical context adds depth to the narrative and informs character motivations 5 diverse characters and perspectives populate your world with diverse characters each with their own backgrounds experiences and perspectives this not only reflects reality but also enriches the narrative by offering varied viewpoints 6 technology and progress consider the level of technological advancement in your world how does technology impact daily life communication and societal structures technological elements can shape the narrative and add layers to your world 7 cultural nuances explore the cultural nuances within your world what languages do people speak what customs and traditions define their societies pay attention to details that showcase the richness of cultural diversity 8 economic realities delve into the economic aspects of your world how do people earn a living what industries drive the economy economic conditions can be a significant factor influencing character motivations and conflicts 9 climate and geography consider the climate and geography of your world these elements impact agriculture travel and the overall lifestyle of the inhabitants natural features also contribute to the atmosphere of the story 10 show everyday life provide glimpses into the everyday lives of your characters what do they eat wear and do for recreation these details add texture to your world and make it more relatable to readers 11 evolution of society explore how societies in your world have evolved over time consider societal shifts advancements and cultural changes that have shaped the present state of affairs this historical context provides depth to your worldbuilding remember that even in a nonfantasy setting the world should serve as a dynamic and integral aspect of your narrative influencing and being influenced by the characters and events in your story

lands where in a panic water flooded his mouth burning his lungs and the magic that permeated in the air around him overwhelmed his senses as somewhere beyond the surf something shifted through the sands the world already declaring war on his unwanted arrival he scrambled onto all fours hair clinging to his face like an unwoven spool of copper wire forcing him to shake the strands out of his face before he could open his eyes where he was met with his own reflection the surface of the water was so still it was almost like glass reflecting the bright azure sky above and the white clouds rolling lazily across it his own reflection stared back at him showing off the darkened hair and clothes that beared down on him a cold breeze skimmed the water brushing across his arms as he sank his hands deep into the pale bleaching sand beneath him the smell of magic filling his nose for a moment dante remained frozen and watched as his shifting hands slid deeper into the sands before a low reverberating roar shook the ground beneath him sending ripples across the water and echoing in his ears a wave of dread soon washed over him twisting in his stomach lifting his gaze dante saw in water ahead figures coming into view first there was one then another and then dozens fifty or more mages some standing some kneeling all bracing themselves but what grabbed his attention was the massive abomination emerging from the sand when it finally broke the surface dante watched the massive creature armored with a thick shelled frame standing on four angular legs bristling with jagged spikes with batted breath its body was a grotesque patchwork of a beige underbelly bright crimson armor on top massive pincer claws mounted on its shoulders and a second set of almost humanlike hands tucked beneath with black flesh peeking through the gaps between its armor the first thing that ran through dantes mind was the tightening in his chest that nervousness which crept in like the water still sitting in his lungs before he could even notice he wasnt ready he knew he wasnt not for this not for what was coming however he wasnt alone at least fifty statesanctioned mages had been sent here by the vile between the normal world and pandora with him unlike him they were all prepped all trained all confident his eyes flicked over the crowd catching their faces in quick desperate glances and slowly it dawned on him the others who were rising stepping forward taking the ground had an even more horrified look in their eyes than he did one person shuffled forward almost standing upright and then jerked back when the creature set its sights on him falling flat on their ass in the sand before shifting slowly shuffling backward wait whatwhy do they look even more sacred than me danta murmured theyre the ones with magic the fear was contagious spreading like wildfire dante could feel it in the air even more so than the mana it was heavy with then it happened someone screamed run their voices cut through everything immediately setting the tone for all those like dante who got lost in the suspense and suddenly nearly half of the mages were running spit flying from their mouths shouts and cries mingling with the crashing of water the scraping of boots over sand terror rippled across the crowd as they scrambled uncoordinated desperate but more importantly helpless the creature remained still only its eyes the black glossy gems embedded into its flat cylindrical head could prove that it was even alive they shifted in every direction trailing their fleeing prey thin sheets of membrane clearing sand from its eyes as two additional eye stalks shot out as dante began lifting himself from the sand in a wideeyed stupor while the mages desperately tried to fight against the water slowly their escape he watched as the creature revealed its hideous maw filled with false armored teeth made from jagged portions of its shell in a thunderous roar that sent most to the ground preparing for an attack that didnt come at least one that didnt come toward them as those who were too close too afraid to run watched as a woman was smashed by its claws her voice cut short as she screamed the blow that came down was so violent dante could hear as her bones shattered and her skin torn while the spray of blood soaked not only the waters more fifteen feet away but the others unfortunate enough to be close by when the creatures claws lifted she lay there partly afloat in the shallow water that quickly stained red before it lashed out and struck the next man ripping him in half dantes heart skipped a beat with an immediate heartwrenching realization these people are supposed to be mages supposed to be more prepared than me what is this wait wwhat am i doing i need to get out of here he thought as dantes body began to instinctually move one person sharing his poor timing came close to him and unknowingly reached out desperately trying to get away and shoved dante down back into the water which splashed up onto his body further soaking his clothes having no time to do anything else but get back up on his feet dante began to move but caught the sight of the creature moving with horrifying speed its legs sliced through the shallow water each step sending splashes and screams into the sky it reached out catching the slowest the sound of bone snapping and flesh tearing made dante flinch and he forced himself forward despite the nausea rising in his throat struggling through the water and sand with sopping wet clothes clinging heavy to his skin that fought against him and a satchel filled with supplies and debris weighing him down he began to sprint blindly as he caught some semblance of a rhythm dante noticed all around him people were shedding boots backpacks even layers of clothing desperate to move faster even still their legs kicked awkwardly beneath them as their bodies fought against water and the sand that simply refused to let go someone beside him soon fell hard ripping at their boots and throwing them away just then another earpiecing scream echoed out of the mouth of another damned mage behind dante and when he turned the world blurred together as he watched the monster crashed down on another person its claws closed around their torso lifted them above his open maw and tore the body split apart so easily dante couldnt bring himself to believe it to be real even still regardless of how he felt the creature emptied out the mages internal organs before dropping the corpse lifelessly into the water blood spilling out in thick clouds that lingered instead of sinking dante couldnt help but freeze and watch too much was happening too fast for him to properly separate his disturbed interest and survival instinct so he just froze and watched sinking into the chaos losing itself in it that was until the blood spread around him warm against his legs staining the water red looking down he pulled his leg from the bloody water and grimaced at the new crimson coat that dyed his pants before something beside him started bubbling not just near him but all across the field yeah okay this is really bad dante whispered now finally gaining his senses something else is coming or that things preparing something either way i need to get the hell out of this water turning his head to glance at the more well verse crowd he saw the same look of panic mixed with a realization that hed missed a man with long black hair tied back into a soaked ponytail gritted his teeth before raising his hand in defiance having had enough the mans body came to life with wisps of mana as he prepared to fight back we gotta get the fuck outta here this things got before the man could finish a turret of water shot up like liquid magma throwing the mans now scorched body almost a hundred feet in the air steam and blood trailed the mans now presumably dead body as it danced in the air before crashing into the ground with a solid splash this things got magic someone screamed we wont be able to escape without nodont another yelled in another violent burst of steam and blood both of them were flung into the air bodies torn apart in an instant and just like that they were gone dantes heart slammed against his ribs watching the mage drop like flies however after maintaining silence for a few moments before regaining his composure he stumbled back into a run realizing this was his chance unlike the mages here he didnt yet have his magic so they were drawing its attention not him and in the show of power the creature managed to trap a cluster of fifteen or so people making it so they were unable to turn their backs and run whether they wanted to or not so they had no choice but to fight and began summoning magic fighting drawing the creatures ire stumbling further away from the now explosive battlefield dante cursed himself as his body still refused to move like hed wanted hed seen what those whod already fled did to get away but he himself got carried away in the chaos moving to fix his mistake he tore the satchel off and threw it aside and quickly had his knife in his hand next he slashed at his pants cutting around the knee ripping fabric away he kicked his boots off hard stripping everything that slowed him down his sweater which hed brought assuming hed be thrown in a cooler climate was next he tried to pull it off failed then drove the knife down the center and ripped it open wrenching it free and throwing it away as he ran the water still resisted him but he was lighter now free enough to gain a sizable distance from the fight however this time he didnt dare turn back having already tested his luck far too much so he ran until the screams faded until the sounds grew distant until there was nothing behind him anymore and only once he simply could not go on any longer did he finally allow his legs to give out he dropped to his knees slamming into the sand coughing and heaving in an attempt to catch his breath once he had he lifted his gaze and saw the biome around him nearly change entirely as bright rainbow colored coral reefs spread beneath the water like forests small fish darted past weaving through stone and color as if nothing of before had happened it was beautiful and it was terrifying dante breathed slowly forcing himself to calm down as the last echoes of chaos disappeared from him and as he looked out into the enchanting expanse he smiled crookedly so this is it he laughed this is pandora his first taste of this world may have been far from ideal however his reason for being here made any emotion that wasnt his excitement and determination simply fleeting and temporary maybe one day ill even get used to it he wondered the thought of what that would take made his chest tighten as he knew that even if this place didnt kill him today it would try again tomorrow and then the next day until itd succeeded after a long moment he muttered aloud voice rough pandora dante rose slowly to his feet as he spoke the water beneath him rippled outwarded as he stood alone in silence as he looked out toward the coral the fish the endless sea my new homestill better than the mage councils prison

gov from 21 to 23 january berik aryn director general of the islamic organization for food security iofs paid a working visit to the lebanese republic opening a new chapter in dialogue on food security and agricultural cooperation in the middle east during the visit mr aryn held meetings with dr nizar hani lebanons minister of agriculture and salim baddoura director general of the department for international organizations at the ministry of foreign affairs of lebanon the talks focused on lebanons growing interest in deeper engagement with iofs and the countrys possible accession to the organization focus on practical benefits not formalities lebanese officials expressed strong interest in the work of iofs emphasizing that any future membership should be built on clear practical outcomes in particular the lebanese side highlighted the importance of developing concept notes that would clearly outline the tangible benefits of potential iofs membership priority areas for projectbased cooperation and mechanisms that could support national food security and agricultural resilience such a pragmatic approach reflects lebanons current challenges in the agrifood sector and its interest in solutions that deliver measurable results rather than symbolic participation kazakhstan and lebanon agriculture as common ground beyond the multilateral agenda the meetings also addressed opportunities to expand bilateral cooperation between kazakhstan and lebanon especially in agriculture the sides discussed prospects for increasing mutual trade in agricultural products as well as strengthening ties between producers exporters and relevant institutions kazakhstans role is particularly notable given that iofs is headquartered in astana positioning the country as a key platform for international cooperation on food security across the islamic world and beyond food security as a regional priority observers note that lebanons interest in iofs reflects a broader regional trend countries are increasingly seeking collective solutions to food security challenges amid climate change supply chain disruptions and geopolitical uncertainty the visit by the iofs director general signals not only lebanons openness to new partnerships but also the growing relevance of iofs as a practical projectoriented organization capable of connecting countries expertise and resources as discussions continue the groundwork laid during this visit may translate into closer cooperation both within iofs and at the bilateral level between kazakhstan and lebanon kazakhstan lebanon

summit held in beijing from october 13 to 14 2025 the global womens summit cohosted by the chinese government and un women was held in beijing chinese president xi jinping delivered a speech and political leaders and renowned womens figures from around the world attended the summit the proposal and organization of this womens summit were to a great extent meant to commemorate and pay tribute to the world conference on women held in beijing 30 years ago in september 1995 the fourth world conference on women was held in beijing china at that time chinese leaders including president jiang zemin and premier li peng as well as un officials and dignitaries from various countries attended the event it was at this very conference that the then us first lady later secretary of state hillary clinton delivered her famous speech in which she declared the globally resonant feminist proclamation human rights are womens rights and womens rights are human rights that speech inspired womens movements around the world the 1995 beijing conference also produced the beijing declaration and the accompanying platform for action setting numerous goals and commitments for the advancement of women in china and across the world this conference had a profound impact on the development of womens causes both in china and globally the hosting of the 1995 beijing world conference on women was not a coincidence in the early 1990s china was trapped in domestic and international difficulties for various reasons the chinese government sought to break the impasse and win economic and diplomatic support including regaining recognition from the western countries that dominated the international order womens issues became an entry point for this effort the founding and development of the chinese communist party ccp and the peoples republic of china have always been closely tied to the womens cause as a longstanding leftist party the ccp has made womens liberation one of its fundamental goals and key agendas during the land revolution workers movements student movements the antijapanese war the civil war between the kuomintang and the ccp the united front work and international propaganda the ccp always used the banners of womens liberation opposition to the bondage and oppression of women and gender equality to gain support from women and progressive forcesan important reason for its rise and eventual victory early female leaders of the ccp such as cai chang xiang jingyu and he xiangning made great contributions to the partys growth and to the advancement of chinese women mao zedong the partys leader famously proclaimed that women hold up half the sky criticized patriarchal and clan oppression and promoted the cause of womens emancipation the very first law enacted after the founding of the peoples republic of china was the marriage law which guaranteed freedom of marriage and promoted gender equality although a series of political upheavals misgovernance and increasingly conservative policy shifts under the ccp later severely damaged womens rights and interests the historical legacy of womens liberation was nonetheless partially preserved this historical background became an important favorable condition for chinas successful bid to host the fourth world conference on women however in the 1990s china remained relatively poor its legal system was underdeveloped public security was unstable and womens rights were frequently violated the trafficking of women and children domestic violence against women rape and sexual harassment girls dropping out of school exploitation and bullying of female workers and suicides of rural women were all common phenomena in china at the time legal and social protections for women were insufficient and womens rights were in urgent need of improvement although china in the 1990s was poor and backward in terms of womens conditions and general living standards it was also more open and more eager to integrate into the world than it is today at that time the world was in the postcold war wave of globalization and china showed its sincerity by enacting the law on the protection of womens rights and interests as a result the united nations western countries and international human rights and feminist movements supported chinas hosting of the fourth world conference on women hoping through this opportunity to expand cooperation with both the chinese government and civil society on womens issues spread feminist ideas in china raise awareness of womens issues and promote both the advancement of womens rights in china and the global womens movement the 1995 beijing world conference on women was overall a success not only did hillary clinton deliver a remarkably progressive speech but burmese democracy leader aung san suu kyi also addressed the opening ceremony and beverly palesa ditsie a black lesbian activist from south africa gave a speech on lgbt rights it was evident that the chinese authorities worked hard to present an open and progressive image chinas organizational capacity and its declared commitment to advancing womens rights were recognized after this conference chinas international image improved and its relations with western countries also saw progress however in the thirty years since then the rights and status of women in china as well as the feminist movement have not advanced smoothly or continuously rather they have experienced twists and turns moving from progress to regression from 1995 to the early 21st century the chinese government indeed promoted several laws and policies aimed at protecting womens rights and publicly advocated for the protection of women and girls while tacitly allowing the development of some nongovernmental organizations focused on womens issues for example the government cracked down severely on the trafficking of women and children greatly reduced the number of girls dropping out of school strengthened the fight against crimes such as rape and saw an increase in organizations focusing on the rights of female workers with economic development womens average income and employment opportunities also increased womens safety rights and incomes improved noticeably at the same time however the chinese authorities remained vigilant and repressive toward nongovernmental feminist forces with strong political overtones and independence only organizations and activists without political or rightsbased agendasthose limited to improving womens economic educational or living conditionswere allowed to operate nevertheless before around 2010 due to economic growth improved living standards and a relatively relaxed political and media environment womens rights did see significant progress after that however womens rights and the feminist movement in china stagnated and gradually regressed around 2010 several highprofile domestic violence cases occurred in which women after suffering extreme abuse and finding no help killed their husbandsyet court rulings favored the male side marking a major setback for the antidomesticviolence agenda which is crucial within feminist advocacy around 2015 the chinese authorities launched a fierce crackdown on feminist organizations and activists several street activists and radical feminists were detained and multiple feminist groups were banned this further narrowed the space for independent feminist activism in china and marked the governments growing intolerance of radical feminist expression it is worth noting that china had already hosted a global womens summit in 2015 during which the authorities monopolization of womens issues and exclusion of independent feminist voices had already become apparent in 2017 and thereafter the global metoo movement swept across the world and reached china the authorities made no official comments and in practice adopted a negative and repressive stance toward the movement in cases such as the one where zhou xiaoxuanxian zi accused tv host zhu jun and others within the system the authorities suppressed online discussions and searches and female accusers and supporters were frequently silenced having their posts deleted and accounts banned the judiciary tended to rule in favor of male defendants while mainstream media in mainland china either ignored or kept silent on these cases progovernment influencers and conservative figures openly disparaged the metoo movement criticizing or even insulting the women who came forward in 2020 amid huge controversy the chinese government enacted the divorce coolingoff period law which undermined freedom of marriage and made it more difficult for women trapped in domestic violence or unhappy marriages to escape the 2021 little red mansion case in shanghai and the 2022 chained woman incident in feng county revealed that despite official claims of having eradicated the trafficking of women the reality was that trafficking and enslavement of women still existed particularly affecting poor rural and disabled women who remain vulnerable to deprivation of personal freedom and abuse meanwhile the number of women in chinas top leadership and official positions has decreased and they have become increasingly marginalized in the past china had several influential female leaders such as soong chingling jiang qing chen muhua and wu yi most of whom held substantial positions of real power in recent years their numbers have dwindled in the current chinese communist partys highest decisionmaking bodythe 24member politburo including its sevenmember standing committeethere are no women at all the highestranking woman in chinese politics today shen yiqin serves only as a state councilor focusing on womens and childrens affairs a rank slightly below that of vice premier women already underrepresented and weak in chinas decisionmaking institutionsespecially at the top levelhave now seen their representation and influence further diminished in recent years the stagnation of chinas womens liberation movement and the regression of womens rights have been the result of multiple interrelated causes first this is an inevitable outcome of the increasingly conservative nature of chinas official system and policies as well as the overall cooling of the countrys political climate in recent years at the founding of the chinese communist party ccp as a revolutionary party it actively promoted womens liberation and mobilized women to join the revolution both to strengthen its own power and to align with its broader revolutionary goal of overthrowing the old world and the three great mountainsimperialism feudalism the confucian agrarian autocracy and bureaucratism however after the ccp took power in 1949 it became a force for constructing and maintaining a new order it thus leaned toward preserving the status quo prioritizing harmony and stability over reform and justice and relying on men who held dominant positions in terms of violence authority and wealth women by contrast were sacrificed and subordinated their role shifted from being liberated to being disciplined in family work and society women were expected to serve the greater good for example during the mao era womens liberation was promoted in name but in reality women who sought divorce were often denied by the courts and some women were even semiforced into marriages with soldiers the allchina womens federation which was originally intended to protect womens rights had no independence at all it was highly subordinate to the party and the state and largely served as an instrument for compromise and social stability maintenance this trend emerged as early as the 1950s when the ccp began transforming from a revolutionary party into a conservative one since then the governing elite of the ccp has oscillated between periods of openness and conservatism but since 2015 the pendulum has clearly swung toward conservatism offline political protests have been completely banned freedom of speech has tightened significantly formerly tolerated moderate civic organizations have been dissolved and many activists have been arrested feminist activists and the feminist movement naturally fell within the scope of this repression the authorities fear that feminism and other progressive ideas could threaten their rule and are wary that feminist groups and other civic organizations could undermine the partys monopoly on power ruling elites inherently prefer to preserve order and suppress those who defy it a conservative system and policy framework inevitably suppress feminism and womens resistance and complaintsjust as conservative governments do around the world second the improvement of womens rights and the development of womens causes in china have entered a bottleneck stage the more progress is made the harder further progress becomes in earlier decades womens rights were extremely poor and crimes against women were overt and severesuch as the trafficking of women frequent rapes and girls being deprived of education at that time both the government and society shared broad consensus and strong motivation to combat such problems and resistance to related campaigns was relatively low however once these severe and visible violations were largely reduced further promoting gender equalityachieving parity in rights economic conditions and discourse power between women and men and enhancing womens influence in the state family and all industriesbecame much harder to gain widespread support for feminists who raise systemic and structural questions about patriarchy in social institutional ideological and resourcedistribution terms threaten the vested interests and established realities of many and are therefore even less likely to be understood or accepted by a maledominated government and society changing such deeprooted realities is also far more difficult naturally leading feminism into a new period of difficulty third maledominated antifeminist forces have been on the rise forming a counterforce that hinders further progress in womens rights the vigorous modern womens liberation movements while challenging traditional patriarchy and advancing gender equality have also provoked male discontent and backlash in issues ranging from domestic violence sexual harassment and marriage to genderbased competition for employment education and social resources when women unite to defend their rights and resist patriarchy many men instinctively react with hostility uniting instead to oppose feminism womens identity politics have in turn triggered mens identity politics in recent years antifeminist men have also become significantly younger and more active online where they possess rhetorical skills that amplify their voices some women too have made extreme or false accusations and such cases have been exploited and magnified by men mobilizing more male opposition to feminism additionally as chinas economy has slowed and social tensions have intensified in recent years gender conflicts have been further aggravated many men especially those from lower social strata who suffer oppression and lack means of resistance redirect their frustrations toward women meanwhile both men and women face similar social hardships but feminists focus more on womens issues which is understandable thereby provoking further male resentment and deepening gender antagonism antifeminist men also use the internet and other platforms to publicly attack feminist women through insults defamation and even by reporting them to their workplaces or schools aiming to punish and silence them for the sake of social stability and out of consideration for male sentiment and grievances the authorities often side with men and further repress feminist activism in recent years cases such as the alleged voyeurism scandal at sichuan university and the alleged sexual harassment case at wuhan university were both handled by officials in ways that favored men and harmed women fourth the global resurgence of conservatism and the rise of rightwing populism have created an unfavorable international environment for feminism which has inevitably affected china as well since donald trump defeated hillary clinton to become us president in 2016 many countries around the world have witnessed a wave of explicitly antifeminist rightwing populist upsurge this trend has weakened external pressure on china to improve human and womens rights and has simultaneously emboldened antifeminist tendencies within both the chinese state and society under these combined influences the chinese governments stance on womens rights has shifted from open and amicable to conservative and austere compared with 1995 when china was poor backward and eager for western and global approval the china of 2025 is far richer and more powerful and its rulers more selfconfident and autonomous they no longer feel compelled to please the west or integrate into the world and thus act more willfully and unscrupulously on womens issues in the eyes of chinas top leadership under xi jinping womens issues are part of the construction of socialism with chinese characteristics for a new era women are seen as screws in the machinery of nationbuildingserving the state society and family and contributing to the realization of the chinese dream and the great rejuvenation of the chinese nation women must obey the overarching political agenda those who refuse to conform to official directives seek independence express themselves autonomously or expose injustices and dark realities faced by women are seen by the authorities as troublemakers who must be suppressed the metoo movement and grassroots feminist activities are regarded as discordant notes disturbing social harmony and must therefore be silenced thus the 2025 global womens summit differs vastly in its stance tone and objectives from the world conference on women 30 years ago whereas the 1995 conference was highly international in character todays summit is steeped in chinese characteristics aligning with the governments recent emphasis on cultural confidence and hosting international events under chinas leadership the resolutions and legacy of the 1995 conference have been selectively and instrumentally appropriated by todays chinese government rather than sincerely upheld or fully inherited the women showcased and honored at this summitsuch as wang haoze zhang guimei chen wei and hua chunyingare all figures within the system or officially endorsed individuals while independent and dissident chinese women are entirely excluded this is unsurprising and reflects the states monopoly over the recognition reward and representation of women who must pledge loyalty to the party and the system at this years summit xi jinping announced a fund of 110 million us dollars to support global womens causes claiming that china would strengthen international cooperation particularly to help women and girls in the global south developing countries in the specifics of these initiatives one can clearly see china emphasizing womens and girls economic and cultural rights while downplaying womens political rights and distinct feminist demands this indicates that china seeks to export its own narrative and model of womens development to other countries in competition with the west at a time when trumpera us policy had cut off much of americas funding for womens and marginalized groups causes worldwide chinas move also serves to project an image of internationalism and openness while competing with the us for global leadership if the chinese model of womens development spreads globally it will be a mixed blessing for womens movements around the world the positive side lies in gaining the financial personnel and policy support of a major power the negative lies in chinas rejection of the liberaldemocratic model of womens empowerment and its potential to export and infiltrate authoritarian norms thereby undermining womens causes founded on universal values and modern feminism as the governmenthosted global womens summit took place in beijing state media such as peoples daily simultaneously denounced grassroots feminism as infiltrated by foreign forces and destabilizing china this shows that the official womens summit not only fails to encourage independent feminist efforts but also uses staterun womens conferences to monopolize representation interpretation and participation in chinas womens issues this monopolization stifles womens voices outside the state framework and inevitably renders chinas womens movement bureaucratic shallow and fragile hindering the development of womens rights and the defense of womens interests chinese womens visibility and global attention remain lower than those of women from some smaller asian african or latin american countries for instance in the bbcs annual list of 100 most influential women chinese faces are rarely seeneven though women from mainland china constitute more than onesixth of the worlds female population this reflects the negative impact of suppressing independent female voices in china of course in order to project an image of representing chinese women and defending womens rights both domestically and internationally the chinese government has invested heavily in this summit and related initiatives this years event will likely yield certain achievements and positive outcomes for china and global womens causes yet compared with the world conference on women 30 years ago its glow is dim the 1995 beijing conferencelike the ccps early genuine contributions to womens emancipationhas now become a signboard used by the current ruling elite to embellish its image and court international goodwill they commemorate its form while discarding its essence and in many specific respects even run counter to it times have changed two womens conferences held in the same city embody entirely different motivations and effects modern chinese women have experienced both suffering and glory their fate full of twists and turns today they again find themselves subject to the currents of history beyond their control the cause of womens liberation in china once made brilliant progress but has also endured many setbacksand its future appears ever more difficult and far from optimistic the author of this article is wang qingmin a chinese writer human rights activist and feminist
